name: N-Desethylprotonitazene

binding.tissue_or_cell: FLP-FRT-HEK hMOR; HTRF cAMP
binding.notes: Data reported for N-desethyl ISOtonitazene (DEI) in Vandeputte 2023 — same N-desethyl moiety; pharmacologically near-identical to N-desethyl protonitazene. EC50 4.13 pM — among most potent MOR ligands ever characterised in vitro.

metabolism.notes: Already an N-desethyl metabolite of protonitazene; further demethylation observed in human hepatocyte incubations.

notes: Sold as a drug in its own right since ~2022 — was both a metabolite and a parent. β-arrestin superagonism (Emax >100% DAMGO) explains why respiratory depression is worse than the analgesic Ki ratio predicts.

name: Nitazene

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Parent unsubstituted 2-benzylbenzimidazole; weak MOR activity relative to alkoxy/halo-substituted analogues. Used as SAR reference compound.

data_gaps_remaining: No published Ki for unsubstituted 'nitazene' parent at human MOR
All published data are for substituted analogues
notes: The unsubstituted parent — rarely encountered. Reference numbers (Kozell, Vandeputte) refer to substituted analogues, not this compound specifically.

name: Brorphine

binding.tissue_or_cell: FLP-FRT-HEK hMOR; HTRF cAMP / Gi pathway
binding.notes: Less potent than fentanyl at binding (Ki ~17× higher than fentanyl 1.4 nM in same assay), but comparable in-vivo potency (rat antinociception ED50 0.0858 mg/kg)

functional.notes: Brorphine analogues do NOT show significant bias vs hydromorphone (Connors 2024 — Neuropharmacology); Emax above reference compound (so-called 'superagonist' for arrestin)

biased_agonism.interpretation: Not significantly biased relative to reference. Brorphine and halogenated analogues recruit β-arrestin2 with high efficacy — at odds with the idea that 'designer opioids are uniformly β-arrestin-biased'.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Full MOR agonist via Gαi/o; high β-arrestin2 recruitment with Emax 209% of hydromorphone but unbiased relative to reference (i.e., both pathways activated proportionally).

metabolism.notes: Hepatocyte studies show oxidative metabolism; primary metabolites are hydroxy-brorphine and the descyclized piperidine ring-opened products.

notes: Piperidine-benzimidazolone scaffold — a bridge between nitazenes (benzimidazole) and fentanyl-like piperidines. Found in supply since 2019; mostly displaced by nitazenes by 2022 but resurfaced 2023.

name: U-47700

binding.tissue_or_cell: rat brain membrane homogenate
binding.notes: Original Upjohn (1978) compound — designed as morphine alternative. ~7.5× more potent than morphine in-vivo despite weaker binding.

binding.tissue_or_cell: rat brain membrane
rat brain membrane
FLP-FRT-HEK hMOR
binding.notes: Full agonist at MOR; rat antinociception ED50 0.405 mg/kg

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Full MOR agonist. Induces ~25% MOR internalisation (similar to DAMGO), in contrast to AH-7921's ~5% (Hsu 2019).

routes.subject_demographics: Male rats, allometric extrapolation to human
routes.notes: Human CL extrapolated 0.944–1.371 L/h/kg via PBPK + IVIVE; no human clinical PK studies exist.

metabolism.notes: Krotulski 2017 — primary metabolite N-desmethyl-U-47700; secondary N,N-didesmethyl. CYP3A4/3A5/2B6/2C19 all contribute.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2C19 PMs likely have reduced clearance; not clinically demonstrated.

notes: Original Upjohn 1978 compound. ~7.5× morphine in-vivo (rat). Was the #1 designer opioid by deaths 2015-2017 before scheduled.

name: U-49900

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Diethylamino homologue of U-47700 (dimethyl → diethyl). MOR agonist per GTPγS in cloned hMOR. Krotulski [35S]GTPγS assay characterised this and seven U-series analogues — U-49900 was a weaker MOR agonist than U-47700.

metabolism.notes: Krotulski 2017 — major metabolite N-desethyl; N,N-didesethyl-N-desmethyl most abundant in urine.

data_gaps_remaining: Specific Ki at MOR/KOR/DOR (only relative GTPγS Emax published)
notes: Direct N-ethyl homologue of U-47700. Less potent functionally; appeared mid-2017 as scheduling workaround.

name: Mt-45

binding.tissue_or_cell: PathHunter CHO cells stably expressing hMOR + β-arrestin2; GloSensor cAMP
binding.notes: MT-45 is uniquely a poor recruiter of β-arrestin2 — see biased_agonism field.

functional.notes: Compare to morphine EC50 5.4 nM in same assay — MT-45 ~240× weaker functionally
EC50 23 μM — i.e., MT-45 is dramatically G-protein biased; very poor β-arrestin recruiter.

biased_agonism.interpretation: MT-45 is strongly G-protein biased — 18-fold weaker β-arrestin recruitment than expected from its cAMP potency. This is the OPPOSITE of the 'biased toward arrestin' narrative; suggests respiratory depression in MT-45 cannot be explained by arrestin-mediated apnea.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: G-protein–biased MOR partial agonist. Also reported NMDA-antagonist activity at high concentrations (associated with reported ototoxicity / bilateral hearing loss — see off_targets).

metabolism.notes: Multiple hydroxylated and dealkylated phase I metabolites identified in human urine (Helander 2018).

off_targets.target: auditory hair cells (mechanism unclear, possibly NMDA-related)
off_targets.clinical_consequence: Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss reported in MT-45 users in Sweden 2014 cluster — distinctive of this compound, not shared with other opioids.

notes: Synthesised at Dainippon (Japan) 1970s as morphine alternative. ~80% morphine-equivalent analgesic potency. Distinctive ototoxicity — unique to MT-45 in opioid class.

name: Ah-7921

functional.notes: Hsu 2019 — AH-7921 induced ~5% MOR internalisation (morphine-like; lower than DAMGO or U-47700).

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Mixed MOR/KOR full agonist. Roughly morphine-equivalent in mouse hot-plate. Lower receptor internalisation than DAMGO/U-47700 suggests biased toward G-protein over arrestin.

metabolism.notes: Vorce 2014 / Karinen 2014 — N-desmethyl is major metabolite in human urine.

data_gaps_remaining: Direct Ki at MOR/KOR/DOR at human receptor
notes: Allen & Hanburys 1970s research compound (the 'AH' prefix = Allen+Hanburys). 0.8× morphine analgesic potency. Cluster of fatalities 2012-2013 Europe.

name: Fentanyl

binding.tissue_or_cell: CHO cells stably expressing hMOR; [35S]GTPγS
binding.notes: Same paper measured IC50 1.23 nM in rat brain (Filizola 2019).

binding.tissue_or_cell: CHO hMOR
binding.notes: Reference value used by Kozell 2024 to benchmark all nitazenes.

functional.notes: log(EC50) = -6.41; not significantly biased vs DAMGO.

biased_agonism.interpretation: Fentanyl is NOT significantly biased compared to DAMGO at the μ-opioid receptor (Ramos-González 2023). Earlier claims that fentanyl is 'arrestin-biased' have not survived re-analysis with operational-model bias factors.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Full MOR agonist. Activates Gαi/o → adenylyl cyclase inhibition, opens GIRK channels, closes voltage-gated Ca²⁺ channels. Also recruits β-arrestin2 and undergoes ~25% receptor internalisation at saturating concentrations.

neuroimaging.finding: [11C]carfentanil PET displacement quantifies MOR occupancy during fentanyl administration in humans; analgesia threshold ~50% MOR occupancy.

routes.notes: Terminal t½ 3-7 h; Vd large due to lipophilicity; context-sensitive t½ ~250 min after 4h infusion.
Apparent elimination half-life is depot-controlled (18-22 h) — much longer than IV t½.

concentration_effect.notes: Plasma 0.5-2 ng/mL = post-op analgesia; ≥3 ng/mL = anaesthesia / respiratory depression begins.

metabolism.notes: Tateishi 1996 — CYP3A4 N-dealkylation is the dominant pathway; norfentanyl is essentially inactive. CYP3A5 contributes minor fraction.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Reduced fentanyl clearance, increased AUC, risk of overdose; FDA black-box warning.
Modest AUC increase for oral / mucosal fentanyl formulations.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP3A4*22 carriers have reduced clearance. OPRM1 A118G (rs1799971) — G-allele carriers need higher fentanyl doses for equivalent analgesia (Park 2007). ABCB1 (P-gp) polymorphisms affect brain efflux.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: MOR internalisation occurs within minutes; receptor recycling t½ ~30 min. Chronic exposure causes desensitisation rather than downregulation.
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Onset 8-24h (transdermal slower), peak 36-72h, duration 7-10 days. Symptoms: lacrimation, rhinorrhoea, mydriasis, gooseflesh, GI cramping, muscle aches, anxiety, insomnia, dysphoria.

off_targets.target: diaphragm / chest wall musculature (chest wall rigidity)
off_targets.clinical_consequence: Rapid IV bolus or high-dose smoked / IV illicit use causes 'wooden chest syndrome' — laryngeal closure + thoracic skeletal muscle hypertonia via central MOR-dopaminergic pathway. Sudden ventilatory failure within seconds-minutes of dose; reversible with naloxone OR neuromuscular blockade.

demographic_differences.sex: Women have ~30% slower clearance than men in some studies (Hess 1985); clinical relevance modest.
demographic_differences.age: Neonates and elderly have reduced clearance (decreased CYP3A activity and Vd changes).
demographic_differences.weight: Obese patients: dosing on lean body mass preferred — Vd does not scale linearly with TBW.
demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Hepatic impairment markedly prolongs t½ (>50% reduction in clearance in cirrhosis).

notes: Reference compound for the class. ~80-100× morphine potency parenteral. Wooden chest syndrome is the #1 acute mechanism of sudden death (especially with very-rapid-onset routes — IV bolus, smoking). Naloxone reverses but high cumulative doses may be required for illicit-route exposures.

name: Carfentanil

binding.tissue_or_cell: Multiple — rat brain (Filizola 2019 IC50 0.19 nM) and human cloned MOR; carfentanil itself used as PET radioligand ([11C]carfentanil)
binding.radioligand_or_probe: [3H]DAMGO; carfentanil also serves as MOR PET tracer
binding.notes: Among the most potent MOR ligands known. Kd 0.024 nM at human MOR (Ramos-Gonzalez 2023). ~10,000× morphine in-vivo.

functional.notes: log(EC50) -8.11; 130× more potent than fentanyl at G-protein activation.
log(EC50) -8.50; 625× more potent than DAMGO at β-arrestin2.

biased_agonism.interpretation: Carfentanil is β-arrestin–BIASED relative to DAMGO (Ramos-González 2023) — opposite of fentanyl. Bias may contribute to apnea / respiratory depression at sub-analgesic doses. Carfentanil also stabilises MOR conformations resistant to naloxone reversal (Faouzi 2024 — see notes).

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Ultra-efficient MOR agonist — full Emax at picomolar concentrations. Carfentanil-bound MOR is sensitive to naltrexone but partially resistant to naloxone and nalmefene (Faouzi et al., bioRxiv 2024 — PMC12198324); has clinical implications for overdose reversal.

neuroimaging.finding: [11C]carfentanil is the standard PET radioligand for quantifying brain MOR occupancy in humans (Bencherif 2002).

routes.notes: Case-report-derived t½ 5.7h for carfentanil and 11.8h for norcarfentanyl (one-compartment model).

metabolism.notes: N-dealkylation to norcarfentanyl (inactive) is dominant pathway; also monohydroxylation of piperidine ring.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Classical opioid; potentially severe due to extreme MOR engagement.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Wooden chest syndrome more frequent and severe than with fentanyl due to extreme potency and rapid onset.

notes: Veterinary use only (Wildnil). ~10,000× morphine in-vivo. Detection in illicit supply since 2016. The β-arrestin bias + naloxone-resistant receptor conformation is a CRITICAL safety message — may need nalmefene or naltrexone instead of naloxone in pure carfentanil exposures.

name: Sufentanil

binding.tissue_or_cell: Cell membrane preparation expressing recombinant hMOR
binding.notes: Lowest Ki of 19 approved opioids in Volpe 2011 uniform ranking — most-potent FDA-approved MOR ligand.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Full MOR agonist. ~7-10× fentanyl potency.

routes.notes: Bovill 1984. Approximately half the elimination t½ of fentanyl.
Sublingual sufentanil (Dsuvia) FDA-approved 2018 for acute pain.

metabolism.notes: Predominantly CYP3A4 N-dealkylation. Desmethyl-sufentanil retains ~10% potency.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Less than fentanyl due to slower iv-titration in clinical use, but possible.

demographic_differences.age: Reduced clearance in elderly and neonates.

notes: FDA-approved 1984. ~7-10× fentanyl. Approved sublingual form for acute pain (Dsuvia). High protein binding (92%) leads to ICU dose adjustments in hypoalbuminemia.

name: Alfentanil

binding.tissue_or_cell: rat brain membrane
binding.notes: Volpe 2011: human MOR Ki 7.65 nM. Lower lipophilicity than fentanyl → faster onset due to high free-fraction at physiological pH.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Full MOR agonist. Fast onset due to pKa (6.5) — 89% non-ionised at pH 7.4, vs fentanyl 9% non-ionised → much more rapid blood-brain transfer per molecule.

routes.notes: Smaller Vd than fentanyl; context-sensitive t½ 47 min after 3h infusion (vs remifentanil 3 min, fentanyl 250 min).

metabolism.notes: Used clinically as CYP3A4 probe substrate.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP3A5*3/*3 (non-expressors) may have slightly reduced clearance.

demographic_differences.age: Reduced clearance in neonates and elderly.

notes: FDA-approved 1986. ~1/4 to 1/10 fentanyl potency but ~3× faster onset and shorter duration. Clinically the CYP3A4 phenotyping probe substrate (alfentanil ER) because >95% CL via 3A4.

name: Remifentanil

binding.tissue_or_cell: rat brain membrane
binding.notes: Slightly more potent than fentanyl at binding. Methyl-ester structure designed to be hydrolysed by nonspecific tissue/plasma esterases.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Full MOR agonist. Ester hydrolysis by nonspecific esterases (not CES1) gives inactive metabolite — terminates effect.

routes.notes: Context-sensitive t½ ~3 min — independent of infusion duration. Cleared by nonspecific blood and tissue esterases; not affected by hepatic/renal failure.

metabolism.notes: Carboxylic acid metabolite — ~1/4000th remifentanil potency.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: BChE genotype does NOT affect clearance — different esterases.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Rapid-onset withdrawal after infusion cessation; opioid-induced hyperalgesia (OIH) is well-documented and clinically problematic.

demographic_differences.age: Reduced infusion rate required in elderly.

notes: FDA-approved 1996. Unique among opioids: clearance by nonspecific esterases (not CYP). Context-sensitive t½ of 3 min regardless of infusion duration — by design. Clinical OIH risk after even short infusions.

name: Lofentanil

binding.tissue_or_cell: rat brain membrane
binding.notes: Among highest MOR affinity of fentanyl analogues. Carfentanil + 3-methyl substitution. Very slow dissociation kinetics — drove its abandonment as clinical anaesthetic (effect duration too long).

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Full MOR agonist. Notable for very slow MOR off-rate.

notes: ~6000× morphine. Janssen 1976. Never reached clinical practice due to extreme duration of action.

name: Acetylfentanyl

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Full MOR agonist via Gαi/o. β-arrestin bias not reliably established for most fentalogs — fentanyl class is broadly unbiased per Ramos-González 2023.

metabolism.notes: Class-default CYP3A4 N-dealkylation pathway shared with fentanyl. Also 4-ANPP (4-anilino-N-phenethylpiperidine) from amide hydrolysis is a marker of synthesis.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: Inferred from fentanyl-class — no analogue-specific human data.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Classical opioid; typically shorter than morphine due to higher lipophilicity.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Wooden chest syndrome — class-shared; rapid IV / smoked / IV illicit exposure.

notes: ~30% of fentanyl analgesic potency (rat hot-plate ED50 0.021 mg/kg vs fentanyl 0.0061). Acetyl group (vs fentanyl's propionyl) reduces MOR affinity. Killed many in 2013-2014 cluster before being scheduled.

name: Benzodioxole-fentanyl

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: 1,3-Benzodioxol-5-yl substituted on N-anilino position. No published direct Ki at human MOR.

metabolism.notes: Methylenedioxy ring may also be cleaved by CYP1A2 (catechol formation) by analogy with MDMA/safrole.

data_gaps_remaining: No published Ki at human MOR
notes: Detected briefly in NPS supply ~2017. Minimal published pharmacological characterisation.

shared_mechanism: Full μ-opioid receptor agonists with structures derived from 1950s Ciba-Geigy analgesic research (original etonitazene). MOR engagement via a binding pose distinct from fentanyl — the 5-nitro group, alkoxy phenyl, and N-dialkylaminoethyl tail all contribute to picomolar affinity. Most subnanomolar in Ki and EC50 at human MOR with Emax 90-110% of DAMGO. NOT detected by fentanyl test strips — chemically unrelated scaffold. Naloxone reverses but cumulative doses ≥4 mg are often needed clinically (vs ≥1 mg typical fentanyl).
shared_pk_summary: Limited human PK. Hepatic metabolism via CYP3A4 (N-deethylation, primary) and CYP1A2 (O-dealkylation of alkoxy chain). Many phase-I metabolites retain MOR activity (notably N-desethyl-isotonitazene and N-desethyl-protonitazene, which are themselves sold as designer opioids). Half-life appears intermediate between morphine and fentanyl (rat data only).
shared_safety: Extreme potency + steep dose-response + onset within minutes of insufflation/IV. Respiratory depression dominates clinical picture. Naloxone is effective but high cumulative doses needed: emergency departments report 4-6 mg cumulative IV naloxone for nitazene reversal (vs 0.4-2 mg typical for morphine/oxycodone). Active metabolites can produce 'renarcotization' as naloxone wears off (t½ 1.5-2.5h) while parent + metabolite persist longer. Public-access intranasal Narcan (4 mg) may be insufficient as single dose. Despite being part of the 'designer opioid' class, evidence does NOT support uniform β-arrestin bias — Vandeputte/Connors studies show MOR-coupling characteristic of full agonists rather than arrestin-biased ligands. The 'biased toward respiratory depression' narrative is better explained by extreme efficacy (Emax >100% DAMGO at full receptor occupancy) plus extreme potency than by pathway bias.
sar_summary: MOR potency rank by 4-position substituent on benzyl: ethoxy ≈ isopropoxy > propoxy > methoxy > butoxy > Cl > F. 5-nitro contributes ~5× potency vs des-nitro analogues. Pyrrolidine (N-pyrrolidino) replacement of diethylamine tail preserves potency but appears to alter MOR/KOR selectivity. N-deethylation of the tail amine produces active metabolites with maintained or even improved MOR EC50. The 2-benzylbenzimidazole scaffold provides a binding mode unrelated to fentanyl's anilidopiperidine — this is why fentanyl-test-strips (immunoassay-based) cannot detect nitazenes.

shared_mechanism: 4-anilidopiperidine scaffold designed at Janssen (1960s) — full MOR agonists with sub- to low-nanomolar Ki at human MOR. β-arrestin recruitment is broadly proportional to G-protein activation (i.e., not biased) per Ramos-González 2023, except for carfentanil which is genuinely β-arrestin-biased. Activate Gαi/o → cAMP inhibition + GIRK opening + Ca²⁺ channel closure.
shared_pk_summary: Extensive CYP3A4 N-dealkylation to inactive nor-metabolite + 4-ANPP marker (from amide hydrolysis). High lipophilicity → rapid BBB transfer, large Vd (3-5 L/kg), context-sensitive half-life that grows with infusion duration (except remifentanil — esterase-cleared). Protein binding 80-92% (albumin + α1-acid glycoprotein). CYP3A4 inhibitors (ritonavir, itraconazole) markedly increase fentanyl exposure; the analogs share the same CYP3A4 N-dealkylation route, but interaction data for individual fentalogs are sparse and the magnitude is not established per-analog.
shared_safety: Chest wall rigidity ('wooden chest syndrome') — class-specific complication driven by central MOR activation via dopaminergic pathway; risk highest with rapid-onset routes (IV bolus, smoked, IN). Reversible with naloxone OR neuromuscular blockade. Onset within seconds-to-minutes; can cause sudden ventilatory failure before classical respiratory depression manifests. Naloxone dose requirements rise with potency: fentanyl typically reverses with 0.4-2 mg cumulative; carfentanil-class exposures may need ≥4-8 mg and/or nalmefene/naltrexone given the unique receptor conformation stabilised by carfentanil (Faouzi 2024).
sar_summary: 4-position substituent on piperidine: methoxymethyl (sufentanil) or methyl ester (carfentanil, remifentanil) markedly increase MOR affinity. N-aryl ring substitution: para-F preserves activity; para-Cl, para-OMe also active; para-thienyl (sufentanil) increases potency. Amide acyl chain: propionyl (fentanyl) > butyryl (butyrfentanyl) > acetyl (acetylfentanyl) > pentanoyl in MOR Ki. Furanyl carbonyl (furanylfentanyl) preserves high potency. 3-methyl piperidine substitution + 4-carbomethoxy (lofentanil) gives extreme affinity + slow off-rate.

class_name: U-series and benzamide opioids (U-47700, U-49900, AH-7921)
shared_mechanism: trans-3,4-dichlorobenzamide + cyclohexyl-diamine scaffold designed at Upjohn 1970s (U-series) and Allen+Hanburys (AH-7921). Full MOR agonists with Ki 11-30 nM at human MOR. U-47700 shows ~25% MOR internalisation (DAMGO-like); AH-7921 shows ~5% (morphine-like) per Hsu 2019. Selectivity: μ >> δ > κ for U-47700; AH-7921 has mixed μ/κ.
shared_pk_summary: Hepatic metabolism via CYP3A4 (and minor CYP3A5/2B6/2C19) → N-desmethyl-U-47700 (active) and further N,N-didesmethyl in urine. Rapid Cmax (rat Tmax 15-38 min IV). Human CL extrapolated 0.944-1.371 L/h/kg via PBPK. Half-life in rats ~2-3 hours; human estimates ~3-5 hours.
shared_safety: Roughly 7-8× morphine potency in-vivo (U-47700). Fatalities reported with combination use, often with benzodiazepines. Naloxone-responsive with standard doses (lower-potency than fentanyl/nitazenes). Not detected by fentanyl test strips.
sar_summary: trans-1,2-diamine geometry is required; 3,4-dichlorobenzamide is optimal — mono-Cl or mono-F reduce potency. N,N-dimethyl tail (U-47700) > N,N-diethyl tail (U-49900) at MOR. Modifications mostly explored as scheduling workarounds 2016-2019.

shared_mechanism: 1-cyclohexyl-4-(1,2-diphenylethyl)piperazine. MOR full agonist with moderate potency (Ki 18-57 nM; cAMP EC50 1.3 μM) but strongly G-PROTEIN BIASED — β-arrestin recruitment is 18× weaker than expected from cAMP potency. Approximately morphine-equivalent in vivo. Not chemically related to fentanyl, U-series, or nitazenes — entirely distinct scaffold.
shared_pk_summary: Hepatic CYP3A4 oxidation; multiple hydroxylated and N-dealkylated metabolites identified in human urine (Helander 2018). No formal human PK studies.
shared_safety: Distinctive bilateral sensorineural hearing loss in MT-45 users (2014 Swedish cluster, 9 cases) — unique among opioids. Mechanism unclear, possibly via NMDA-related off-target activity. Classical opioid respiratory depression also; naloxone-responsive.
sar_summary: Class so small (MT-45 + 2F-MT-45 + a handful of analogues) that no broad SAR. The ortho-fluorine in 2F-MT-45 markedly increases potency (cAMP EC50 42 nM vs 1300 nM for MT-45) and restores β-arrestin recruitment to DAMGO-like potency.

shared_mechanism: 1-(piperidin-4-yl)-2,3-dihydro-1H-benzimidazol-2-one scaffold with arylethyl tail. Functional bridge between piperidine (fentanyl) and benzimidazole (nitazene) chemistries. Full MOR agonist with high β-arrestin2 recruitment (Emax 209% hydromorphone) but NOT biased (G-protein and arrestin scale proportionally). Halogen series (chlor-, brom-, iodo-rphine) all active; bromo (brorphine) is the marketed compound.
shared_pk_summary: Hepatic CYP3A4 — multiple oxidative metabolites in hepatocyte studies. No formal human PK.
shared_safety: Found in supply since 2019. Fatalities reported in US/EU. Naloxone-responsive but potency exceeds morphine. Not detected by fentanyl test strips. Resurgence post-2023 after initial decline.
sar_summary: Para-halogen on arylethyl phenyl ring: H << F < Cl ≈ Br ≈ I at MOR. The 'orphine' parent (no para-halogen) is much weaker.
